relevance_note: This is a case report of SSADH deficiency: "Genetic testing revealed a homozygous mutation in the aldehyde dehydrogenase 5 family member A1 (ALDH5A1) gene", describing the infant, her mother and her sibling; no TNFAIP3 variant is mentioned anywhere.
method_note: Read the full text by hand; no script transcribed anything (there are no tables in this paper, so no stacked cells). I checked every span character by character against the paper with a search tool, because this PDF conversion left non-breaking spaces (U+00A0) at several joins (for example after 'substitution' before 'at chr6:24505155', after 'levetiracetam,' before 'sodium', after 'despite' before 'resuscitation'); those spans reproduce the non-breaking space (written as \u00a0 in this JSON). Where the exact characters around a sentence join were uncertain, I shortened the span to a contiguous fragment I could verify (for example the MRI rows quote 'with normal cortex, white matter, cerebellum, and ventricular system' and 'The brain showed normal myelination adequate for age' without the following '(Figure 1)' phrase). Individuals: the single unnamed patient of this case report (label 'patient', rule 5), her mother and her sibling. The sibling is a relative described in relation to the patient who died at one year with severe convulsions and was never tested ("Genetic testing was ordered for her at that time but unfortunately was not done due to financial reasons"), so she gets an individuals row but no variants row. The father is mentioned only as one of "Her parents" ("Her parents were first-degree cousins") with no individual-level fact of his own, so I gave him no row; this is my main judgement call. Consanguinity 'yes' is recorded for the patient and for the sibling, who had the same parents. Only one variant is printed, the patient's "homozygous mutation G->A substitution\u00a0at chr6:24505155"; the paper prints no cDNA or protein HGVS, no variant class, no pathogenicity classification and no ACMG criteria, so those fields stay 'not reported' rather than being derived from the printed string. Zygosity 'homozygous' comes from the authors' own phrase 'homozygous mutation' about this patient. 'Akaboshi et al. predicted this mutation to cause an abnormal protein translation...' is recorded under functional_evidence_statement as a prediction, not an assay. No parental variant testing is reported, so inheritance is 'not reported'. Death: vital_status 'deceased' for the patient, cause 'respiratory failure' from the case narrative (the abstract's wording is 'leading to fatality'); age at death P4M is recorded only because the paper calls her a "four-month-old female infant" and she died during that same admission, and the same span supports age_at_last_evaluation. treatment_summary lists only treatments I could quote (thiopental and the ventilator are therefore not listed). No HPO identifiers are given because I was not sure of them. No tables have a source column, so source_reference_in_review is 'not reported' for everyone; no earlier report of these patients is cited. Contradictions inside the paper: none found.
